title: Evaluation of Sirs, Mews, and qSOFA Scores to Predict ICU Admission and 14- and 30-Day Mortality in Patients with Hematological Malignancies and Sepsis or Septic Shock
content: Introduction: In hospitalized patients, the risk of mortality in patients with hematological malignancies, related to sepsis and septic shock are high, can be assessed using the Modified Early Warning Scoring score (MEWS). Currently, different tools that predict deterioration have been introduced into clinical practice in hospitals around the world. It remains unclear which screening tool for mortality in patients with hematological malignancies is best. The aim of this study was to evaluate the mortality predictive performance of four sepsis-based scores (i.e. Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS) criteria, and quick Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) in comparison with the more general MEWS score in hospitalized sepsis patients. Methods: We conducted a retropective study. Patients with hematological malignancies and sepsis or septic shock, between January 2017 and August 2020, were included. Suspected sepsis was defined as blood culture collection and initiation of intravenous antibiotics. Outcome was defined as in-hospital mortality within 14 days and 30 days after the sepsis episode or until death. Predictive performance was expressed as discrimination (AUROC) and calibration using the highest You-den index fit test. In addition, the sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value, and positive predictive value of four scoring systems were calculated. The scoring systems were compared with McNemar's test and AUROC by DeLong's method. Results: A total of 775 with sepsis were included in the institution. Of these, 329 (42.5%) patients had diagnosis of hematological malignancies and were included in the study, of which mortality was 89 (27%) at 14 days and 126 (38.3%) at 30 days. Regarding AUROC, qSOFA and MEWS showed higher accuracy than SIRS. However, qSOFA showed low sensitivities for score ≥2, while MEWS low specificities with score ≥4. Conclusions: MEWS seems to be a better choice of score in this study population, shows higher sensitivity than qSOFA and higher AUROC than SIRS for prediction of ICU inter-nation and 14- and 30-day mortality in patients with hematological malignancies and sepsis.
